previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, and peripheral artery disease was admitted for fevers, diarrhea, and a worsening rash. He had a history of calciphylaxis and a chronic left leg ulcer. During admission, the leg wound was found to have necrotizing fasciitis, requiring surgical debridement and a wound VAC. He was treated with piperacillin-tazobactam for polymicrobial infection. A possible aortic valve vegetation raised concern for endocarditis, but TEE ruled it out. He underwent left femoral artery stenting for inflow stenosis. Hypertension was difficult to control and required multiple medication changes, including adding minoxidil and a clonidine patch. His hand pain was attributed to microvascular disease. He improved clinically and was discharged home on IV antibiotics, wound VAC care, and revised medications, with follow-up planned for wound closure and transplant management.

and significant peripheral vascular disease. For primary FSGS

No clear other offending medications or exposures. Patient

# FEVER, resolved

# HYPERTENSION, better controlled 
Profoundly difficult to control hypertension requiring six 
agents
to manage. SBP of 200 mmHg on admission, in the setting of not 
having yet received all home anti-hypertensives. He was 
continued on home labetalol, nifedipine, minoxidil. His 
clonidine patch was increased from 0.1mg to 0.2mg weekly. His

# HISTORY OF NECROTIZING FASCIITIS LLE with exposed Achilles 
tendon
# CALCIPHYLAXIS
# CHRONIC HAND WOUNDS
# PERIPHERAL VASCULAR DISEASE
No evidence of super-infection. Patient follows with Vascular 
outpatient. LLE wound demonstrates granulation tissue of muscle 
with persistently exposed tendon. Plastics surgery is concerned 
around exposed tendon and plans to see patient outpatient for 
this. Wound vac was discontinued and dressing changes should be 
preformed wet to dry daily. He had duplex ___ this admission 
given previous left SFA stent which showed patency. He should 
continue to receive sodium thiosulfate outpatient for presumed 
calciphylaxis. His chronic wounds are likely due to severe PVD. 
His fingers and toes are at risk for autoamputation but nothing 
to do now per surgical consultation. He is to follow up with 
vascular and plastics outpatient. Continued statin and aspirin. 

# CHRONIC PAIN 
Continued acetaminophen 1000 mg q8h. Dosed reduced gabapentin to 
100mg QD per worsening renal function. Reduced oxycontin to 20mg 
BID given reduced renal function. Patient in agreement with pain 
medication down titration. Continued nortriptyline.

===================
- Transplant nephrology will follow up on DSA and BK viremia 
sent this admission. 
- Transplant nephrology will closely follow patient outpatient 
for antihypertensive management and follow up of Cr.
- Please ensure patient follows outpatient with plastic surgery 
and vascular surgery. Dressing for LLE is wet to dry daily.
- His spironolactone and thiazide were held given reduced renal 
function. His oxycontin was decreased to 20mg BID given reduced

- He was transfused 1U PRBcs during hospitalization for chronic
